convoLines.text: "What's the worst thing you've done since the sky changed? Give it time."
No judgment in their face. "We're all doing math that doesn't add up. You're still here. That counts."
"This one — Bitter Leaf. Leaf, stem, smell. You won't forget it now."
"a burned farmhouse — I'll show you on the map sometime. It's real."
"Still on the worst thing you've done."
"Someone should watch your back. Might as well be me."
"...I should say, I trade in what I know. My knowledge for yours. Or food, if you're short on secrets."
"You want to know about that? Okay." "The whole fire was arguing about Hummice last night — what to even CALL it. 'Big-Eyes' got shouted down. What's your vote?"
"Take your time."
"I'm staying out of the naming fight. For now. Someone always gets precious about their pick."
"The fire'll settle it. It settles everything, eventually."
"I should go. You know where to find me."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"This was good." They mean it.
I'm not proud. I'm alive. Those two things stopped overlapping a while ago.
"I've been the outsider so long I forgot what inside feels like. I think I'm remembering."
They go very still. Not relaxed-still. Held-still.
"I don't have to explain myself to you." Sofia stands. "Ask around. See who trusts you after."
"Sure. I'll be around."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Can we talk?" Asher sits down near you. "Just... talk. Like people used to."
"Come get air with me. I need to think out loud."
"Here. I made an extra." Asher presses something into your hand — a decent tool, oiled and kept. (Useful. Keep it.)
The ground remembers.
Names, named.
You watch who eats with whom, who laughs a little too loud at whose jokes. Nothing solid. Keep looking.
You say nothing. The silence sits at the fire with everyone else.
The moot is called. The fire gets built up.
Counted.
"Well. My social battery is officially dead."
They fill the quiet. "Anyway — where was I?"
"What do you make of all this? Really."
"Bleak. Probably true. I keep looking for the part where it's not."
"Nightlight — A soft green glow under the water. It hunts at night — give the dark a wide berth."
"Still on what you make of all this."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"You want to know about that? Okay." Watch what I do, not what I say. That's where the proof is.
"Back home I was invisible. Here, someone might actually see me. I need that to be true."
"Just... if you see me do something well, say so. I know how that sounds. I don't care."
"Anyway — I should get going."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"We never finished talking about what they want — we left it mid-thought, 7 days back. 'A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.'"
"Come get air with me. I need to think out loud."
At the ridge the ground is torn up. Something was here, recently, and it wasn't careful. Michael's hand finds your sleeve. You leave together, faster than you came.
"This one — Bittersweet Nightshade. Leaf, stem, smell. You won't forget it now."
"a spring that runs clear — I'll show you on the map sometime. It's real."
"Proving yourself never ends. That's the secret. You just get better at the proving."
"I'm not asking for a medal. I'm asking for a chance to matter."
"Still on what they want."
"Anyway — that's my cross to carry. What's on your mind?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "They took you — Riddle Me This, on the screens. The whole fire watched. Nobody knew where to look."
You show them White Oak Acorns — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
"Alright. Catch you later."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"This was good." They mean it.

"We never did finish talking about trading knowledge — that was 10 days back. Still on your mind? '...I should say, I trade in what I know. My knowledge for yours. Or food, if you're short on secrets.' We still owe what's been happening a proper ending, too."
"Walk with me? I want another pair of eyes on something."
Asher shows you where they go to think. "Don't tell the others. Everyone needs one place."
"You want to know about that? Okay." "Last time things were different. They always are." "Riddle Me This. They just... took you. Came back like nothing happened. It wasn't nothing."
"I wish there was more to tell. That's it."
"...I should say, I trade in what I know. My knowledge for yours. Or food, if you're short on secrets."
"Good question." "You're family now. Chosen family — the kind that actually counts." "Make of that what you will."
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
"Still on each other."
You show them Bittersweet Nightshade — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
"Yeah? What's up? But what do I know."
"Good question." "Being buried somewhere unnamed." A pause. "Stupid, maybe. But there it is."
"I should go before I say something sincere."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Hey — I found some White Oak Acorns today. You were right, it was right where you said."
"Saw things with too many joints. Give them room. That's the whole lesson."
"Anyway." A small smile.
"Still on that plant lesson."
They hear the warmth in it. They're not ready to let it in.
"Yeah? What's up?"
"You want to know about that? Okay." "Huh. I answered that once — back when the answer was simpler." "You saw it too, right? The Pit. Tell me I didn't imagine the lights."
"We'll see what the treeline brings. We always do."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Sure. I'll be around."
"It's been a while. Glad we circled back to what's been happening."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
Asher: "Hey — come here. You should hear this."
"This one — Chickweed. Leaf, stem, smell. You won't forget it now."
"a spring that runs clear — I'll show you on the map sometime. It's real."
"I keep dreaming about rows of pods. Humming. Tell me I'm not the only one."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up? It'll pass."
"Huh. Let me think about that." Whatever did this — it had a reason. Reasons can be found. That's what I believe.
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"Still on what they want."
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"Thanks for listening. Most people change the subject."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"You called this the end of the world. We're still here, though. That's either something, or it's us."
"Walk my trap line with me? Extra hands, extra eyes."
"Here. I made an extra." Michael presses something into your hand — a decent tool, oiled and kept. (Useful. Keep it.)
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Sure — what's on your mind?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "You feel that? The air before a storm. That's the village right now."
"That's the whole of it. Sorry."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
"Still on what's been happening."
"Anyway — I should get going."
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
"...Actually, forget it."
"You said there was something you regretted. You didn't want to get into it. I won't ask. Just — are you carrying it any lighter?"
"I see." They take a moment to think about your answer.
"an old trapline — I'll show you on the map sometime. It's real."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Walk my trap line with me? Extra hands, extra eyes."
"Here. I made an extra." Asher presses something into your hand — a decent tool, oiled and kept. (Useful. Keep it.)
"Still on that personal stuff."
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
"Good question." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "Everyone's choosing sides and pretending they aren't. I hate it."
"That's... pretty much all of it, honestly."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Okay. We'll pick this up later."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."

deathBeat: d8: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. Evelyn Meyer is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
d8: 🕯️ Evelyn Meyer is dead — the arena. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
recoverHome: d9: That night, they bring Evelyn home. Nobody asks you to help carry; nobody has to. By morning the grave is dug by the fire, and the body is laid out beside it. The filling of it is yours.
systemVoice: d8: SYSTEM: "Perimeter violated! This is unprecedented! ...Is this unprecedented? Checking. Yes. Unprecedented."
d8: SYSTEM: "INTRUDER REPELLED. The pantry’s aroma is now classified as a defensive liability. The audience is chanting the defenders’ names. Fan clubs are forming. This is how it starts."

d8: ◈ THE SPARK — something clicks. A trick Elena learned long ago suddenly has edges it never had. SYSTEM: "ANOMALY: organic unit demonstrates pattern recognition. Slot capacity increased. We are taking notes." (Ability slots: 3)
d8: ◈ AUDIENCE TRIAL — SYSTEM: "The audience wants an encore. A trial, then — smaller this time, but televised." Haul 1,000 kcal to the pantry within 3 days. Reward: integration, and a lesson.

d8: ◈ ARC III — ENGINES. SYSTEM: "VIEWERSHIP MILESTONE. Organic unit demonstrates compounding capability. Resonance protocols unlocked." — Your gifts deepen. Used in sequence, they resonate. The village is no longer just surviving. It is becoming something.

d8: ◈ SYSTEM: "RATINGS DIP. The audience wants STAKES — pointed ones. A PALISADE. Stockpile 14,000 kcal, 350 wood and 60 stone. Walls make such good television. You will thank us when the teeth come."
d9: ⬢ SYSTEM: "Neural depth 53. I can hold more of you now — ability slots: 4."
d9: SYSTEM: Identification complete. You are 0.3% less lost.
d9: SYSTEM: Naming things. Very human. The audience approves.
d9: SYSTEM: Codex and inventory overlay online.

d10: ⬢ SYSTEM: "Neural depth 65. I can hold more of you now — ability slots: 5."
